title: First game fully developed with AI
author: D217K
selftext:
And actually my first post as well, so let's see... 

  
A bit about me: I'm a web-dev and an AI / automations engineer. I know web development practices and languages very well plus have a basic understanding of python. That means I can code a bit and can definitely read and understand code but absolutely have no capability (and time) to develop a game. However, I find myself pretty creative and have a couple of game ideas I would've loved to realize for some time. 

  
A few years back, there was a browser-game about building a data broker company with more or less shady practices where you have to acquire and trade data. Unfortunately, the game never made it out of beta and I cannot remember the name anymore.

  
However, I always liked to play it so I thought I want to build something on top of that base idea (No bare copy of course, that wouldn't be fun). Here's how it went:

I used Claude code from the app. Actually, I did the entire project from my phone without ever touching a computer (yet, I will obviously have to when / if I want to release it as mobile app) which was part of my personal challenge. So, Claude did all of the code, Gemini did most of the artwork (the art that wasn't coded) and I used Godot as engine because I read about it on Reddit and wanted to try it and learn about it. 

  
I have to say, the process went pretty smooth. I told Claude the main idea and first let it make a phase planning. Then, we went through every phase. Claude coded everything, I checked, revised, and sometimes added new functionality, then we proceeded to the next step. I added my Gemini API key in the environment of the Claude code project so that Claude can use the Gemini API to directly generate the artwork. I added github as allowed domain so it can fetch Godot. My own repo was connected so Claude could commit and push. 

Finally, it gave me a zip to upload to itch.io. I played the game, noted down everything I found and we did a correction cycle. In the end, this turned out much nicer than I had expected but maybe I am biased just because it was fun to do. If you want to try it, feel free and let me know what you think.
